transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I feel a little embarrassed even being here, to be honest. I hope I'm not taking up time from people who have real problems. 

It's just... well, I work as a host at a restaurant, and I guess I've just been a bit stressed lately. I just can't seem to stop focusing on my hairline, and the way my face looks under those harsh restaurant lights. I just feel like I look so... old and strange. I know it sounds terribly vain, and my coworkers are always telling me they don't see what I'm talking about at all. So I'm probably just making a big deal out of nothing, but it's been really hard to get it out of my head. 

I'm sorry, does that make sense? Is it okay that I came in for something like that?
Is it mostly your appearance that's been bothering you, or are there other things as well?

Um, no, I... I think it's really just this. Just the appearance thing. I mean, everything else in my life is... is actually pretty good. I don't have any other big problems or, you know, anything serious going on. 

It's really just this one... silly fixation I've gotten stuck on. I hope that's alright? I don't want to sound ungrateful or anything, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for, and I really do like my job. It's just... this one thing about my face and my hair is taking up so much of my energy lately, even though I try not to let it. 

Is that... does that sound like the kind of thing you usually help people with?
Has this preoccupation with your appearance been affecting your ability to do your job or engage in social activities?

Well, I try really hard to keep it separate. I pride myself on being a good host, I really do. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest—and I hope this doesn't make me sound completely irresponsible—it has been getting a little in the way lately. 

I've actually... well, I've been written up at the restaurant. It's just that sometimes I get so stuck in the mirror trying to fix my hair or worrying about how my face looks that I end up being late. Or, um, I'll even miss shifts entirely because I just can't bring myself to go in and stand under those lights. I feel terrible about it, I really do. 

And socially, um, I've kind of stopped doing things, too. Like, I refuse to be in any of the staff photos anymore, and I've stopped going to gallery events or weekend hikes with my friends. I just... I can't handle being seen that way right now. I know I shouldn't let something so vain affect my whole life, and I'm really trying to do better. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Do you believe that your appearance is actually abnormal or unattractive, even when others tell you that it's not?

Um... well... I guess I do. I mean, I know my coworkers say I look fine, and I really, really appreciate them trying to be nice. They're such sweet people. But... when I look in the mirror, I just... I see it. It looks so obvious to me. 

I know I shouldn't think that way, especially when people are trying to reassure me. I don't want to seem like I'm calling them liars or anything! It's just... I really feel like they're just saying it to make me feel better, you know? Because what I see just looks so... wrong. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds terrible and stubborn of me. I really am trying to listen to them. Is it normal to feel like that, even when people tell you otherwise?
Do you think you would feel better about your appearance if you could change the thing that bothers you, or would you still be worried about how others see you?

Um... that's a really good question. I... I think I'd feel better? Like, if I could just fix this one specific thing, maybe I wouldn't worry so much. 

But... honestly, I don't know for sure. I mean, I hope I'd feel better, but sometimes I wonder if I'd just find something else to be embarrassed about, or if I'd still think people were... looking at me funny. I really hope that's not the case, because I'd love to just go back to normal and be a good host again without all this stress. 

Does that make sense? I'm sorry I don't have a better answer for you. I'm just not entirely sure how I'd feel if it actually changed.
Do you think your perception of your appearance is based on how you actually look, or is it something that you feel regardless of your actual appearance?

Oh, um... wow, that's a really deep question. I... I honestly don't know for sure. 

I mean, to me, it feels like it's exactly how I look. Like I'm just seeing the reality of what's right there in the mirror. But... when you put it like that, and since everyone else is always telling me they don't see what I see... maybe it is just a feeling? 

I really try to be objective, I promise I do. But it's just so hard to tell what's actually there and what's just my own... I don't know, my own insecurity anymore. I'm sorry, I wish I could give you a clearer answer. I want to be helpful. I hope I'm not being too confusing... is it okay that I don't really know how to separate the two?
How often do you think about your appearance during the day?

Um... well, it's... it's a lot, honestly. I don't want to sound like I'm obsessed or anything, because I really do try to focus on my job. I love greeting the customers and making them feel welcome. But... 

I guess I think about it pretty much all the time. Especially at work. The lights in the restaurant are just so bright, and I can't stop thinking about how my hairline looks under them... and just my whole face, really. I worry I look old and, I don't know, strange? 

I know my coworkers say I look fine, and I really, really appreciate them, but... it's just always in the back of my mind. Sometimes the front of my mind. I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't be so focused on it when I'm supposed to be working. Is it... is it bad that it's on my mind that much? I really am trying to push past it.
Do you feel like your worries about your appearance are causing you a lot of emotional pain or distress?

Um... yeah, it... it does cause some distress. I don't want to make a big deal out of it, because I know there are people with much worse problems, but... it's been a little hard lately. 

I've actually... well, I've been written up at the restaurant a couple of times. I've been late, or I've had to miss shifts because I just... I couldn't get myself looking presentable enough to go in. I feel terrible about it because I really pride myself on being reliable for the team. 

And I've sort of... stopped doing some of the things I used to enjoy. Like, I don't go on hikes with my friends anymore, or to the local gallery events. I even avoid the staff photos at work. I just... I can't handle the thought of people seeing me, or worse, having it captured on camera looking like this. 

I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't let it affect my life this much. I'm really trying to do better, I promise. Do you think... is it normal to let something like this get in the way of work and friends? I just hope I'm not being too weak about it.
Do you think people are judging you or noticing your appearance even when you're not actively thinking about it?

Um... wow, that's... that's a really good question. I don't want to sound paranoid or anything, because I know people have their own lives and their own problems to worry about. But... 

I guess... yeah, I do kind of feel like people are noticing. Even if I'm trying really hard to just focus on my job and be cheerful, I'll catch someone looking in my direction and I just... I immediately think they're looking at my hairline, or how tired my face looks. 

I try to tell myself they're just looking at the menu, or waiting to be seated, but it's hard to shake the feeling that they're judging how I look. I know that probably sounds incredibly self-centered, and I really don't mean to be. I just... I worry that my appearance is making them uncomfortable. 

Is it... is it bad that I think that way? I know I should just assume the best of people. I really try to be positive, I promise. I hope that makes sense... I'm trying to be as honest as I can.
Do you think your appearance is abnormal or unattractive even when you're not looking in a mirror?

Um... yes, definitely. I know I kind of touched on this a minute ago, but... honestly, that's the whole reason I'm here talking to you today. Even when I'm nowhere near a bathroom mirror, I just... I can't stop thinking about it. 

I constantly picture how my hairline and the rest of my face must look, especially under those bright restaurant lights. I just have this image stuck in my head that I look so old and strange. And like I said earlier, my coworkers are so kind, and they tell me they don't see what I'm talking about at all. I really, really try to believe them, because I don't want to be difficult or seem like I'm brushing off their kindness. I want to be a good sport about it.

But the feeling just doesn't go away, even when I can't see my reflection. It's just always playing in my mind. I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself a bit... I just want to make sure I'm explaining it clearly for you. Am I doing okay answering your questions? I really want to be helpful.
Do you think you would still worry about your appearance if you were completely alone and no one could see you?

Um... gosh, I guess I haven't really thought about it quite like that. I... I suppose I probably would still worry, yeah. Even when I'm just home alone in my apartment, the thoughts don't really just... turn off. I still feel like my hair and my face are just... wrong, even if nobody is there to see it. 

I try really hard to distract myself, though! I'll clean, or watch a show, or read, just so I'm not sitting there dwelling on it. I know it's probably pretty silly to be upset about how I look when it's just me in the room. I really don't want you to think I just sit around feeling sorry for myself all day, because I really do try to keep my mind off it and be productive. 

Is that... does that answer your question okay? I'm sorry if that's not exactly what you were asking, I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think you would worry about your appearance more because of how you think you look or because of how others might judge you?

Um... wow, that's another really thoughtful question. I... I guess I'm not entirely sure how to separate the two, to be honest. 

I mean, I definitely worry about what other people think, like I mentioned with the customers at work. I just don't want to make anyone uncomfortable or be a distraction. But at the same time, even when I'm alone, I still feel so... bothered by how I look. So maybe it's both? Or maybe I just haven't really figured out which one is worse. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm not giving you a very clear answer here. I really want to give you exactly what you're looking for, but I just... I'm not entirely sure which one drives it more. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I don't have a perfect answer for that one. I can try to think about it more if you need me to!
Do you think you would still feel anxious about your appearance if nobody was around to judge you?

Um... yeah, I think so. I mean, I know we just talked about being alone, and... well, even if I knew for a fact that no one was ever going to see me or judge me, I think I'd still feel just as anxious about it. 

It's like... the feeling is coming from inside me, not just from worrying about other people, if that makes sense? Even if I was completely isolated, I'd still know that my hairline and my face look the way they do, and that thought just really upsets me. I try so hard not to let it get to me, I really do. I don't want to sound like I'm just obsessed with myself or anything. 

I hope I'm not just repeating myself too much and wasting your time. Is that the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to understand what's going on with me.
Do you think your anxiety about your appearance would decrease if you were able to correct the specific flaw you're concerned about?

Um... gosh, I really don't know. I guess I haven't let myself think too much about actually fixing it, like with a procedure or something. I mean, maybe it would help? But... I also worry that if I somehow fixed my hairline or my face, I might just... I don't know, find something else to be upset about, or it still just wouldn't look right to me. 

I definitely don't want you to think I'm someone who's just looking for a quick fix or wants to get a bunch of cosmetic surgeries, you know? I know that's probably not a very healthy way to handle things, and I really do try to be reasonable and grounded about all this. 

So, honestly, I'm just not sure if it would actually make the anxiety go away. I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm striking out on giving you a solid yes or no on these last few questions. Is it okay that I don't really know the answer to that? I want to be as helpful as possible, so I can definitely try to think on it more if you need me to!
Do you think your perception of your appearance is based on reality or is it something that you feel regardless of how you actually look?

Oh, um... wow. That's... I guess I really don't know for sure. I mean, to me, it feels incredibly real. When I look in the mirror, the things I see with my hairline and my face, they're just... they're right there. But... I also don't want to sit here and sound like I'm completely out of touch with reality, you know? I know I'm probably making it a much bigger deal in my head than it actually is. I try really hard to be rational about it. 

So... maybe it is just something I feel, regardless of how bad it actually is? I'm honestly not entirely sure how to separate the two. I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or irrational. I really do try to keep a level head about things, especially at my age. 

Is it normal to not really know the answer to that? I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm being a terrible patient today with all these "I don't know" answers. I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly. Am I giving you enough to go on, or should I try to explain it differently?
Do you think you would still feel self-conscious about your appearance if you were in a situation where you knew everyone around you genuinely liked and accepted you?

Um... gosh. That's a really good question. I... I want to say that it would help, you know? Like, if I knew for an absolute fact that everyone just completely accepted me, maybe I could finally relax about it. But... honestly? I think I'd still feel just as self-conscious. 

It's like... even if they were the nicest, most accepting people in the world, I'd still be sitting there thinking, "They're just being polite. They can still see how awful my hairline and my face look." I'd probably just feel guilty that they had to look at me, to be honest. 

I really try not to be that insecure, I promise. I know it sounds like I'm just constantly looking for things to be miserable about, and I don't want you to think I'm ungrateful for people's kindness or anything like that. I work as a host at a restaurant, so I'm around people all the time, and I really do try to put on a brave face and be positive. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very healthy mindset to have. Does that make sense, though? I hope I'm not coming across as too negative or difficult. I just want to make sure I'm giving you an honest answer.
Do you think your anxiety about your appearance is more about the specific features you're unhappy with or about how those features might affect how others perceive you as a person?

Oh, um... wow. That's a really deep question. I guess... well, I'm not entirely sure I've ever really stopped to separate the two in my head. 

I mean, I definitely get fixated on the specific things, like my hairline and my face. But... maybe it really is more about how people see me? Working at the restaurant, I'm the first face people see when they walk in, and I just... I want to make a good impression. I want people to think I'm put-together and capable. And I worry that when they look at me and see those flaws, they're judging me as a person, you know? Like they think I'm sloppy or that I don't take care of myself, which really isn't true at all. I try very hard to be presentable.

But I also don't want to sound like I'm completely obsessed with what everyone thinks of me. I know I shouldn't care so much about other people's opinions, and I really do try to be my own person. I hope I don't sound too vain or superficial saying all this. 

Is it okay that I don't have a clear-cut answer for that one either? I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. Am I on the right track with what you're asking?
Do you think your appearance is abnormal or unattractive to the point where it's not based in reality?

Oh, gosh... "not based in reality" sounds so severe, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think I'm completely delusional or anything like that. I try so hard to be logical and grounded. 

But... I guess the whole reason I'm here is because I just can't stop thinking about it, even when I try to reason with myself. Like, when I'm at work, the way my face and my hairline look under those harsh restaurant lights... I just feel like I look so old and, I don't know, strange? It's all I can focus on. 

But then—and this is where I guess the reality part comes in—my coworkers tell me they genuinely don't see what I'm talking about. I try not to bring it up too much because I don't want to be a burden or seem vain, but when I have mentioned it, they act like I'm seeing things that just aren't there. 

So... maybe my view of it isn't entirely based in reality? I really do try to believe them, I promise I do, because I want to be rational about this. I hope admitting that I still struggle to see what they see doesn't make me sound completely crazy. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think your anxiety about your appearance would decrease if everyone around you assured you that they liked and accepted you as a person, regardless of how you look?

Oh, um... well, we did sort of touch on this earlier, but... gosh, I want to say yes. I really do. I want to be the kind of person who can just accept a compliment and feel good about it. 

But... I think even if everyone went out of their way to tell me they liked me for who I am, I'd still be stuck in my own head about my face and my hairline. I'd probably just think they were taking pity on me, or that they felt bad for me. 

I know that sounds terrible, and I really try not to be that cynical. I appreciate people's kindness so much, especially the customers and my coworkers at the restaurant. I just... I don't think their reassurance would be enough to make the anxiety go away completely. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm repeating myself a bit, and I don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm not trying to get better. Is it okay that I still feel that way? I hope I'm not being too difficult or frustrating to work with.
